assessment: Assessment Submission Guide. Students should upload coursework through the official learning portal before the deadline shown on the course page. The system records the time of submission and displays a confirmation message when the upload is complete. Students should keep that confirmation until the instructor has graded the work. Files should normally be submitted as PDF documents unless the assignment instructions specify another format. A file should be named with the course code and student identifier, but passwords and other private credentials must never be included in a filename. Late submission is normally penalized according to the course instructions. However, a student who experiences illness may request an extension if suitable medical evidence is provided to the course coordinator before the deadline. This exception is not automatic, and the coordinator must confirm the decision. A student should not assume that sending an email alone counts as a successful upload. If the portal is unavailable, take a screenshot of the error without exposing private information and contact the help desk as soon as possible. Keep the original file and check that the uploaded version opens correctly. Group assignments should identify all group members in the location specified by the instructor. Do not upload a draft when the final version is required. If the course page and a general guide appear to conflict, follow the current assignment-specific instruction and ask the instructor to clarify the difference. These rules are synthetic examples for this lab, not real university policy.
it_password: Account Recovery and Password Safety. A user who forgets a password should begin at the sign-in page and select the recovery link. The recovery system sends instructions to the registered email address when that address is valid and associated with an account. Follow the link promptly because recovery links may expire. After access is restored, choose a unique password and do not share it with classmates or support staff. Never send a password or recovery code in an email, chat message, screenshot, or public issue tracker. If a recovery message does not arrive, check the spam folder and verify that the correct email address was entered. Repeated requests may cause a short waiting period. If the account may have been compromised, contact the help desk and explain what happened without sending secret credentials. The help desk may ask for non-secret information to verify account ownership. A recovery code should be treated like a temporary password and stored privately. Do not assume that a similar-looking message is genuine; inspect the sender and use the official sign-in page rather than an unexpected link. If the registered email is no longer accessible, use the documented identity-verification process. Password reset instructions can change when the service changes, so consult the current official IT guide. This document is synthetic teaching material and does not describe a real institution's systems.
returns: Damaged Parcel Support Procedure. Customers who receive a damaged parcel should contact the support team within 48 hours of delivery. The customer should attach clear photographs of the damaged item and the outer packaging, including the shipping label when it is safe to do so. Keep the item and packaging until support explains the next step. The support team may ask for the order reference and a short description of the damage. Do not post addresses, phone numbers, or order details publicly. The 48-hour reporting window applies to the synthetic Pakistan-region policy used in this exercise. A separate sample policy for another region has a 72-hour window, so the region must be checked before giving advice. A change-of-mind return is different: unused items may be returned within 14 days under the synthetic example, subject to the listed conditions. A damaged-item report should not be incorrectly processed as a change-of-mind return. If photographs cannot be uploaded, contact support and record the case reference. The support agent should confirm whether a replacement, repair, or refund is available; the chatbot must not promise a specific outcome. If the packaging appears unsafe or contains a leaking substance, avoid direct contact and follow appropriate safety guidance. Retain support correspondence until the case is resolved. All time windows and procedures in this document are invented for educational use and are not a real company's terms.
workplace: Remote Work Eligibility. In this synthetic workplace guide, employees may request remote work with manager approval. Approval depends on the role, information-security requirements, team coverage, and the employee's signed agreement. Contractors are different from employees: contractors may work remotely only when the signed contract explicitly permits remote work. General employee guidance must not be used to override this contractor condition. A manager should review the relevant agreement and confirm the applicable arrangement before making a decision. Staff should use approved devices and protect confidential work from public view. Remote access must follow the organization's security instructions, and credentials must not be shared. If an employee's request is denied, the manager should explain the operational reason and any available alternative. A contractor who cannot find the remote-work clause should ask the contract owner rather than assume permission. The guide does not establish employment rights or replace legal advice. The audience and document version should be checked before retrieving a passage, because similar wording may exist in separate employee and contractor documents. An access filter can help select the correct audience in a prototype, but it is not a security system. Confidentiality and authorization must be enforced by the actual application. This synthetic guide exists only to demonstrate retrieval and exception handling in a lab.
printer: Printer Troubleshooting Guide. If a printer has power but produces blank pages, first check whether the device displays a warning or error. Check the ink or toner level, confirm that the correct supplies are installed, and run the printer's cleaning utility if the device manual recommends it. Print a test page after cleaning to determine whether output has improved. Do not disassemble the printer while it is connected to power. If the test page remains blank, inspect the selected printer and print queue, then check whether the document itself contains visible text. A scanner that creates a blank image requires different checks: confirm document placement and choose the correct scanning source. Do not apply scanner instructions to a printer simply because both devices produce blank output. Record the device model and error message before contacting technical support. Some models have different maintenance menus, so use the manual for the exact model. If the device is under warranty, avoid steps that the manufacturer says may invalidate it. Keep the steps in order and stop if a warning says the action could damage the equipment. A useful troubleshooting response identifies the device, preserves the warning, and presents the relevant steps together. This is synthetic instructional text for retrieval experiments and is not a substitute for a real device manual.
